title: Bench rows stack three glass planes; ink-3 there is 6.25:1, unmodelled
body:
## Summary
In the dossier's bench, a hovered or self row lays glass on the bench's glass on the dossier's gradient, and `.bd-bench-score` in --bd-ink-3 measures 6.25:1 there, under the 7.0 floor check-contrast asserts for that rung. The checker scores single planes only, and the dossier's own gradient is typed, not a token it reads.

## Description
examples/hirelane/design/check-contrast.mjs:106-123 models one plane per surface (glass on ground, glass-2 on ground, card top on void). The dossier paints `linear-gradient(180deg, rgb(255 255 255 / 7%), rgb(255 255 255 / 3%))` over --bd-ground (examples/hirelane/components/board/style/level2/l2-dossier.css:29), typed rather than read from a token, so the checker's "glass-2 on ground" coincides with the dossier's top stop by value and would not follow a retune of either. Inside it, `.bd-bench` adds --bd-glass (l2-dossier-2.css:143), and `.bd-bench-row:hover` / `[data-self="true"]` add another --bd-glass (l2-dossier-2.css:175, :180). On that three-plane stack --bd-ink-3 (#aeaeb9) is 6.25:1 and --bd-ink-4 4.58:1; `.bd-bench-score` (l2-dossier-2.css:211) is 15px ink-3, which the checker's own rule holds to AAA. The parallel fix for the carousel card landed this morning (the slide's stops became --bd-slide-top/--bd-slide-foot, read by the checker); the dossier is the un-migrated sibling. Fixed: the dossier's stops become tokens the checker reads, the checker composites the stacked planes the bench draws, and the self/hover row either drops its second glass or sets its score in --bd-ink-2.

## Flow
- open a dossier -> hover a bench row, or look at the candidate's own (self) row
- the score figure on that row is ink-3 on glass over glass over the dossier's 7% top stop -> 6.25:1
- node design/check-contrast.mjs -> ok --bd-ink-3 7.81:1 on glass-2 on ground (the stack is not modelled)
- build order: tokens for the dossier's two stops; SURFACES gains "bench row on bench on dossier top" composed from tokens; watch ink-3 go UNDER at 6.25; then retune the row (one glass, or ink-2 for the score)

## Expected impact
A reader comparing bench scores reads the self row's figure at AAA like the rest of the room; the checker stops passing a stack it cannot see. Could break: the bench's self-row emphasis if the second glass is dropped, so the accent border has to carry it alone.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every ink-3 figure meets the 7.0 floor on the surface it actually sits on
Before: 6.25:1 (ink-3 on glass 4% over glass 4% over white 7% over #0a0a0c), computed with the checker's own formula; checker reports 7.81:1
After: >= 7.0:1 predicted with one glass on the row, or 8.35:1 with ink-2 on the score (computed)
Method: simulation - ratios computed from the tokens; the instrument (stacked surfaces in check-contrast.mjs) is outside this context's paths and the bench needs a browser to confirm the stack
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: design/check-contrast.mjs SURFACES gains the dossier's top stop (from new --bd-dossier-top/--bd-dossier-foot tokens) and the bench row stack (glass on glass on that stop); ink-3 must go UNDER at 6.25:1 on the base tree before the row is retuned; a browser look at the bench in hover and self states

title: The register summary is nowrap and wider than a phone's foot
body:
## Summary
`.bd-register > summary` is `white-space: nowrap` and carries the presence reading, the capability count and the gated count on one line; at 390px wide that line is wider than the foot, and nothing lets it wrap or scroll.

## Description
examples/hirelane/components/board/style/chrome/the-foot.css:83-86 sets `.bd-register > summary { list-style: none; white-space: nowrap }` and the summary holds three spans (components/board/shell/Foot.tsx:87-95: "Athena is not connected", "16 capabilities offered", "3 gated") plus the ::after glyph, with --bd-s2 gaps, --bd-s4 side padding and the gated span's --bd-s3 inset. At --bd-text-sm (15px) that is roughly 55 characters, about 400-460px, while the root at 48rem pads by --bd-s3 (responsive.css:124-126), leaving about 366px at 390. `.bd-register` is `margin-inline-start: auto` in a wrapping flex row, so it drops to its own line but cannot get narrower; `.bd-root` does not clip inline overflow, so the page scrolls sideways. Fixed: let the summary wrap below a container width (or drop the presence reading to its dot), keeping the pill at --bd-control.

## Flow
- open / at 390x844 (or any container under ~30rem)
- the foot's register pill is wider than the content box -> horizontal page scroll, or the pill's end is cut off
- fix: an @container bd-root (max-width: 30rem) rule that lets the summary wrap and grow in block size

## Expected impact
A phone reader sees the whole capability sentence without a sideways scroll. Could break: the register body's upward offset (`inset-block-end: calc(var(--bd-control) + var(--bd-s2))`) assumes a one-line summary, so it has to follow the pill's real height.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - no horizontal overflow from the foot at phone width
Before: estimated 400-460px summary in a ~366px content box at 390px (character count x average advance)
After: 0px overflow predicted with a wrapping summary
Method: simulation - widths estimated from the copy and the tokens; measuring needs a browser at 390x844, which this round may not run
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a browser probe at 390x844 reading the summary's scrollWidth against .bd-foot's clientWidth and document.scrollingElement.scrollWidth against innerWidth, red on the base tree, green with the wrap rule

title: The carousel's dots are 7px targets at a 15px pitch
body:
## Summary
Each `.bd-dot` is a 7x7 button 8px from the next, so its target is 7px and its centre pitch 15px - under WCAG 2.5.8's 24px and under the 44px reach target this direction commits to for every other control.

## Description
examples/hirelane/components/board/style/level1/l1-carousel-2.css:98-109 sizes `.bd-dot` at --bd-dot (7px, tokens.css) with `padding: 0` and `.bd-dots` gaps them by --bd-s2 (8px). They are real buttons (components/board/Carousel.tsx:268-281), each jumping the loupe to a named candidate. tokens.css's --bd-control comment says the direction commits to ONE reach target (44px) and names the level rail and filter as the controls that were under it. WCAG 2.5.8's spacing exception needs a 24px circle per target that does not overlap its neighbours; a 15px pitch fails it. The arrows beside them are 44px and reach every card, so the "equivalent control" exception may hold - which is why this is a call, not a defect. Fixed (if wanted): an invisible hit area (a ::before inset to 24px) with the pitch widened to 24px, the 7px mark unchanged.

## Flow
- L1 carousel with five or more candidates -> the dot row under the rail
- pointer or touch on a dot -> a 7px target; a near miss lands on the neighbour or nothing
- decide: keep (arrows are the equivalent) or widen the pitch to 24px with a ::before hit area

## Expected impact
Touch and low-precision pointer users can jump to a candidate directly. Could break: the dot row grows from about 15px to 24px per candidate, about 9px x N wider.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - each dot is a reachable target
Before: 7px target, 15px centre pitch (7 + 8), read from the sheet
After: 24px hit area at a 24px pitch (predicted)
Method: probe - sizes read from the sheet; whether the arrows count as the equivalent control, and how wide the row may grow, is a design call that needs the rail seen in a browser
Result: better
Gate: direction

title: Mono figure lines track at 0.02em and 0.04em, off the tracking scale
body:
## Summary
`.bd-mono` sets `letter-spacing: 0.02em` and `.bd-slide-meta` sets `0.04em`; the scale the direction aliases has -0.03em, 0, 0.06em and 0.12em, so both are typed values off the scale, and they disagree with each other.

## Description
examples/hirelane/components/board/style/level0/l0-board-2.css:140 (`.bd-mono`, the monogram) and examples/hirelane/components/board/style/level1/l1-carousel-2.css:39 (`.bd-slide-meta`, the slide's mono meta line) each type a tracking value. design/hl-scales.css declares --hl-track-tight (-0.03em), --hl-track-normal (0em), --hl-track-wide (0.06em) and --hl-track-caps (0.12em); tokens.css aliases tight and caps only. DESIGN-LAW §1.2 makes type a closed scale; check-law reads px and colours, so em passes. Fixed: either alias --hl-track-wide as --bd-track-wide and use it on both (a visible change: 0.04 to 0.06, 0.02 to 0.06), or name a mono tracking step in tokens.css with its reason.

## Flow
- L0 pile monograms and the L1 slide meta line, side by side
- both are mono figures, tracked differently and off the scale
- decide the step, then a sheets test like the font-size one holds letter-spacing to tokens

## Expected impact
The two mono figure voices track alike and move with the scale. Could break: monograms in a tight pile (24px visible) may crowd at 0.06em.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - tracking from the scale, one value for one voice
Before: 2 typed tracking values, 2 different, 0 on the scale (grep of letter-spacing outside tokens.css)
After: 0 typed values (predicted)
Method: probe - the count is read from the sheets; which step is right is a typographic call that needs the monograms seen in a browser
Result: better
Gate: direction

title: Twin pills dim to different opacities when disabled: 0.38 and 0.3
body:
## Summary
A disabled `.bd-btn` drops to opacity 0.38 and a disabled `.bd-arrow` to 0.3, two typed numbers for one state on controls cut from the same round-pill recipe.

## Description
examples/hirelane/components/board/style/level2/l2-dossier-3.css:27-30 (`.bd-btn:disabled { opacity: 0.38 }`) and examples/hirelane/components/board/style/level1/l1-carousel-2.css:87-90 (`.bd-arrow:disabled { opacity: 0.3 }`). Both are pills at the reach target with round corners and the same hover family (test/sheets.test.ts reads them as one recipe). The disabled state has no token, so each control chose its own. Fixed: one --bd-disabled step in tokens.css, read by both, with a sheets test that every :disabled opacity reads it.

## Flow
- L1 at the first candidate: the Previous arrow is disabled (0.3)
- L2 with an act unavailable: the bar's button is disabled (0.38)
- decide the one value, then pin it with a token

## Expected impact
One disabled look across the room. Could break: whichever control moves changes legibility slightly (disabled controls are exempt from contrast, but 0.3 of ink-2 on glass is faint).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one disabled state, from a token
Before: 2 values for 1 state (0.38, 0.3)
After: 1 token (predicted)
Method: probe - the count is read from the sheets; which value is right is a visual call
Result: better
Gate: direction
evidence:
examples/hirelane/components/board/style/level2/l2-dossier-3.css:27-30  .bd-btn:disabled { opacity: 0.38; cursor: default; }
examples/hirelane/components/board/style/level1/l1-carousel-2.css:87-90  .bd-arrow:disabled { opacity: 0.3; cursor: default; }
